questions.prompt: Why is `ctx.Products.FromSqlInterpolated($"... WHERE Price > {minPrice}")` safe from SQL injection?
options: EF Core strips quotes from `minPrice` before inserting it
The interpolated values are automatically turned into SQL parameters
Interpolated strings can only contain numbers
`FromSqlInterpolated` runs the SQL in a read-only transaction
questions.explanation: With `FromSqlInterpolated`, the values in the interpolated string are automatically turned into SQL parameters; the other safe option is `FromSqlRaw` with explicit `DbParameter`s.

questions.prompt: What does EF Core send to the database for `_appContext.Tasks.ToList().Where(t => t.IsCompleted)`?
options: `SELECT * FROM Tasks;`, and the `Where` filter then runs in memory
`SELECT * FROM Tasks WHERE IsCompleted = 1;`
Nothing until the `Where` result is enumerated
One query per task to check `IsCompleted`
questions.explanation: `ToList()` runs the query first, so all rows are loaded into memory and `Where` filters them locally as an `IEnumerable`. Keeping it `IQueryable` would push the filter into SQL.

questions.prompt: How does EF Core detect that someone else changed a row since you read it?
options: It reloads the row before every `SaveChanges` and compares all columns
It locks the row from the moment it is read
It includes the concurrency token in the `UPDATE`/`DELETE` `WHERE` clause; if 0 rows are affected it throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`
It always throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` when two users save the same entity, even without a token
questions.explanation: EF Core only throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` if a property is a concurrency token: the token is in the `WHERE` clause, so a changed row means no match, 0 rows affected, and the exception.

questions.prompt: What is the downside of marking just `Name` with `.IsConcurrencyToken()` instead of adding a `[Timestamp]` `RowVersion`?
options: It can't be used with SQL Server
It only detects changes to `Name`, not to other columns
It makes every update overwrite silently
It requires `ExecuteUpdateAsync` for every update
questions.explanation: A normal property marked as a concurrency token only detects changes to that property. SQL Server updates `RowVersion` whenever any field changes, so checking that one column detects all changes.

questions.prompt: Projects have a `RowVersion`. You bulk-update them with `ExecuteUpdateAsync`. What happens to concurrency checking?
options: EF Core checks `RowVersion` automatically and throws on conflicts
EF Core loads each project first to compare versions
The update fails, because `ExecuteUpdateAsync` can't run on entities with a `RowVersion`
It is skipped; you must put `RowVersion` in the `Where` clause yourself if you need it
questions.explanation: `ExecuteUpdateAsync` bypasses tracking, so `RowVersion` is not validated and no `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` is thrown. For concurrency safety with bulk updates, include `RowVersion` in the `Where` clause manually.
